claims.statement: BPE repeatedly counts adjacent symbols, merges a highest-frequency pair, adds a symbol and saves ordered merge rules.
claims.scope: Character/subword adaptation of BPE; the shown fence performs one merge only. Row boundaries are this toy's convention; original paper uses word boundaries. Full training has a chosen merge budget and implementation-specific stopping rules.

Frequency counts, stable selection, bounded training, writing ordered codes and updating statistics.
Code-file order becomes merge rank; encode applies earliest available rank, with nonoverlap and no-pair termination.

review_questions.question: Sorting and ties?
review_questions.answer: Counter ranks by count, equal counts retain first encounter. Fixed input order is stable; official subword-nmt has a different stable secondary rule. No universal tie rule claimed.

review_questions.question: Overlap, boundaries and termination?
review_questions.answer: Count sees all adjacent positions; merge consumes nonoverlapping positions left to right, separately per row. i grows1or2, so finite. Original fence is one step; full BPE uses explicit budgets and source-specific stop criteria.

review_questions.question: Lengths and vocabulary definition?
review_questions.answer: Per-row token occurrences2/3 differ from4/4 letters; initial vocabulary3 plusab means4 types. Exercise lengths4/3/4; oldabac sequence changes without changing count.
